jobs.title: Mid-Career Software Engineer
jobs.description:

In a world where technological threats move at unprecedented speed, CHAOS Industries delivers advanced sensing and detection solutions that give the ultimate advantage: time.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised $1B in total funding from leading investors including 8VC, Accel, and NEA. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, and London. For more information, please visit www.chaosinc.com.

CHAOS is seeking a highly-skilled and motivated Senior Radar Software Engineer to join our team supporting our R&D and product engineering initially focusing on our next-generation radar products. Work full-time on-site in our office in Los Angeles (El Segundo), California

Bachelor’s or higher Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related degree
5+ years of experience in professional, object-oriented software development
Extensive/advanced Python experience
Experience with Agile lifecycle processes including Scrum, Continuous Integration, and Test-Driven Development Methodologies
Ability to work with minimal supervision and collaborate on small teams
Solid understanding and extensive experience in software development using Linux
U.S. Person status is required as this position will require the ability to access U.S.-only data systems

Development experience in Ground or Airborne Sensors (Radars, EO/IR, EW, etc.)

Current or previous DoD security clearance
Experience with Networks (software and hardware)

Experience developing near-real-time, embedded SW

Experience with additional languages such as C++, Rust, NodeJS, Java, Go, etc.

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer - New Grad
jobs.description:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.
About the Team The Machine Learning team builds the model-side techniques that make SambaNova’s platform fast and capable. We train speculative decoding models that accelerate inference, develop efficient ML methods such as quantization, sparsity, and distillation, and build agentic systems on top of our foundation model serving stack. Our work spans research, applied science, and production, from novel approach design to proofs of concept and shipping to product. Reinforcement learning and post-training are within our scope and a growing part of our roadmap.
About the Role As a new grad Machine Learning Engineer, you’ll train and evaluate models that make large language models cheaper and more capable to serve. Depending on your interests, that could mean training speculator (draft) models and tuning acceptance rates, compressing models without losing accuracy, or designing and evaluating agentic workflows for tool use, planning, and long-horizon tasks. You’ll work closely with the AI performance, compiler, and runtime teams to turn research results into measured end-to-end wins, and you’ll have room to pursue open problems as our reinforcement learning and post-training work ramps up.
Responsibilities Train, evaluate, and tune speculative decoding models (Dspark/Dflash, Medusa/Eagle-style heads, and multi-token prediction) to increase acceptance rates on production workloads.
Develop and implement optimization techniques, including quantization, sparsity, distillation, pruning, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning, to quantify the trade-offs between model quality, latency, and resource efficiency.
Build and evaluate agentic systems: tool calling, multi-step planning, retrieval, and long-context reasoning on top of our serving stack.
Design rigorous evaluations and benchmarks; make accuracy and quality claims that hold up under scrutiny
Translate recent research into working implementations, and run ablations to understand what actually drives the result
Partner with the AI performance, compiler, runtime, and product teams to ship model improvements into SambaNova products
Contribute to emerging areas such as reinforcement learning, post-training, and reward modeling as the roadmap expands

Required Qualifications B.S. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
Strong programming skills in Python
Solid foundation in machine learning, linear algebra, probability, and numerical computing
Hands-on experience with PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX
Working knowledge of transformer architectures and the LLM training or inference pipeline
Ability to design a clean experiment, interpret results honestly, and communicate findings clearly

Preferred Qualifications M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field

The Systems Software Test Engineer contributes to developing, executing, and documenting automated tests that verify end-to-end system functionality, robustness, and reliability in accordance with approved test plans, procedures, and defined metrics. Collaborates with Systems Test and Systems Engineering to review product requirements, feature designs, system robustness and reliability metrics, and system configurations, and develops test cases for system verification with appropriate guidance.
Develops and maintains automated test suites using established test automation frameworks and approved verification procedures.
Executes and monitors automated test suites through CI/CD pipelines; reviews test results, metrics, logs, and artifacts; investigates failures using established procedures; and escalates suspected product defects.

per hour. Base pay will vary based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience and may also fluctuate depending on candidate’s location and the overall job market. In addition to base pay, Tandem offers a competitive compensation package that includes bonus and a robust benefits package.

.

Machine Learning Engineers
at IMC play a pivotal role in building the systems that drive training and deployment of large-scale ML models across IMC's global operations. They collaborate with quantitative researchers, hardware specialists and software engineers to build robust systems that get the most out of GPU acceleration, distributed computing and the broader open-source ML ecosystem. ML Engineers' work directly shapes how fast we can experiment, iterate and deploy — accelerating the cycle that turns a research idea into a live trading strategy.

This is a unique opportunity to solve problems at the intersection of advanced machine learning and trading, where your contributions will shape the future of IMC's technology and trading capabilities.

As a team, our Machine Learning Engineers broadly work across two areas: ML Research Engineering
, focused on the systems and frameworks researchers use to train, evaluate and iterate on models at scale; and ML Performance Engineering
, focused on making ML workloads execute as efficiently as possible, typically through GPU and low-level systems optimization. These aren't rigid tracks, and there is overlap between them. You will bring depth of expertise in at least one of these focus areas and collaborate closely with global team members.

Your Core Responsibilities

The responsibilities below are representative of the role — the exact mix depends on your team, area of expertise and location.

ML Research Engineering

Develop large-scale distributed training pipelines that manage complex datasets and models.
Partner with quantitative researchers to automate ML experiments, hyperparameter tuning and model retraining.
Work with HPC specialists to optimise workflows, improve training speed and reduce compute cost.

ML Performance Engineering

Build and optimise low-latency inference pipelines, ensuring models deliver real-time predictions in production systems.
Maximise performance in training and inference using GPU hardware and acceleration libraries.

Across both areas

Extend and improve the internals of machine learning frameworks and open-source tools to raise their performance for our workloads.
Design scalable model infrastructure capable of handling high-volume trading data and delivering real-time, high-accuracy predictions.
Evaluate and roll out third-party tools that enhance model development, training and inference capabilities.

Your Skills And Experience

Core, regardless of focus area:

3+ years of experience in machine learning, with a focus on training or inference systems.
Production software engineering — Python, testing discipline and genuine ownership of systems once they ship.
Machine learning fundamentals — you understand modern ML workloads beyond high-level APIs and can reason about model behaviour, correctness and performance at the level relevant to your area of expertise.
A systems mindset — you reach for measurement before opinion on performance, scale or reliability issues, and can make sound build-versus-buy decisions.
Strong collaboration — comfortable explaining the reasoning behind your technical decisions, working through differing perspectives with researchers and adapting your approach when the evidence supports it.

Depth In One Or More Of The Following

Distributed training and large-scale systems — parallelism strategy, data pipelines and checkpointing; frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow or JAX.
GPU performance and low-level optimisation — reasoning about memory, compute and latency at the device level, and optimising performance across kernels, compilers and hardware (e.g. CUDA, Triton or equivalent).
Production inference systems — hands-on experience building and hardening real-time, low-latency prediction pipelines in high-performance environments.
Numerics and correctness at scale — low-precision effects, KV caching, batching, and knowing which optimisations stay bit-exact.

Technologies listed above are examples rather than requirements; equivalent depth developed using other stacks or hardware platforms is equally relevant.

Also a Plus

Exposure to cloud platforms and orchestration tools.
A track record of contributing to open-source projects in machine learning, data science or distributed systems.

Not sure this is the one?
If your strength is mainly in modelling and research direction, our Deep Learning Researcher roles are likely a closer fit. If your strength is in general infrastructure rather than ML-specific systems, take a look at our broader infrastructure engineering roles.

Base salary is only one component of total compensation; all full-time, permanent positions are eligible for a discretionary bonus and benefits, including paid leave and insurance. Please visit Benefits - US | IMC Trading for more comprehensive information.

IMC is a research-driven trading firm where quantitative modeling, machine learning, and engineering shape how modern markets are traded. A stabilizing force in markets since 1989, we provide liquidity across trading venues, delivering the best outcome in value and risk management to investors. Using our own technology and capital, we build proprietary systems and algorithms that operate across global markets. Our researchers, traders, and engineers work as a collective, combining rapid experimentation, advanced infrastructure, and real-time feedback to turn insight into execution and execution into advantage.

As AI agents increasingly act autonomously on behalf of individuals and businesses, from booking services and accessing APIs to executing financial transactions, companies need infrastructure that can determine which agents are legitimate, who they represent, what actions they're authorized to perform, and whether their behavior presents a security or fraud risk.
Our client is building real-time verification and decisioning infrastructure that enables businesses to safely interact with AI agents at scale.
The platform combines agent identity verification, behavioral intelligence, risk assessment, and security controls to distinguish legitimate automated activity from suspicious or malicious behavior.

We're looking for an exceptional Machine Learning Engineer to build the models that distinguish a trusted AI agent from an attack, in real time and under load.

This is an opportunity to join a small, highly technical founding-stage engineering team and take meaningful ownership of mission-critical ML infrastructure.
What You'll Be Working On
The models behind this platform operate directly on the production request path. They must evaluate activity and support trust decisions in real time, under the same strict latency constraints as the rest of the infrastructure.
There is no offline batch job to hide behind and no second chance if a prediction is too slow or incorrect.

You'll work on problems involving:

Real-Time Fraud & Threat Detection:
Develop ML models that identify potentially fraudulent, malicious, or unauthorized agent activity while minimizing false positives.
Behavioral & Anomaly Detection:
Identify suspicious patterns, anomalous agent interactions, and emerging risks across automated transactions and API activity.
Low-Latency ML Inference:
Build and optimize production model-serving systems capable of making accurate decisions under demanding latency and throughput requirements.
Cold-Start & Low-Label Learning:
Develop effective detection approaches when labeled examples are scarce, including unsupervised learning, weak supervision, and custom evaluation datasets.
End-to-End ML Ownership:
Build, evaluate, deploy, monitor, and continuously improve production ML systems, from data and feature pipelines through real-time serving.
Adversarial ML:
Help build systems that remain effective as malicious actors adapt their behavior to evade detection.
Agentic AI Infrastructure:
Work at the intersection of modern ML, AI agents, tool calling, identity verification, and security.

What We're Looking For

Must-Haves

3+ years of professional ML experience
, ideally 5+ years, building, evaluating, and deploying production models, not just research or notebooks.
Strong Python and a modern ML framework (PyTorch or TensorFlow); solid SQL.
Production ML systems end to end: feature pipelines, training, evaluation, and low-latency, real-time serving.
Comfort with low-label and cold-start problems, including anomaly detection, unsupervised methods, weak supervision, and building evaluation sets and labels from scratch.
Data analysis, statistics, and experiment design.
Strong software engineering. You ship versioned, testable, reproducible code, not throwaway models.
Experience working in highly technical engineering environments with strong software engineering standards.
Ability to take ownership, solve ambiguous problems, and ship production-grade solutions in a fast-moving startup environment.

Strongly Preferred

Applied ML in fraud, risk, abuse, account integrity, or security.
Experience building ML models for fraud prevention, threat detection, trust and safety, or other systems designed to prevent malicious activity.
Graph ML / GNNs, sequence or behavioral modeling, or anomaly detection.
LLM / NLP work, and familiarity with AI agents, including tool use, function calling, and MCP.
Experience in adversarial settings, where the threat evolves against the model.
Explainable, auditable, reproducible ML, with real model versioning.
Experience developing ML systems at highly technical, engineering-driven companies, particularly those working on large-scale infrastructure, payments, fraud prevention, cybersecurity, or AI platforms.

Bonus Qualifications

Payment protocols (x402), agent identity (DID / VC), or crypto commitments (Merkle anchoring).
Experience at an early-stage startup or building ML infrastructure from the ground up.
Familiarity with real-time transaction monitoring, behavioral risk scoring, or identity verification systems.

San Francisco, CA.

Company Description

Vitol is a leader in energy and commodities. Vitol produces, manages and delivers energy and commodities to consumers and industry worldwide. In addition to its primary business of trading, Vitol is invested in infrastructure globally, with $10+billion invested in long-term assets.

Vitol’s customers include national oil companies, multinationals, leading industrial companies and utilities. Founded in Rotterdam in 1966, today Vitol serves its customers from more than 40 offices worldwide. Revenues in 2025 were $343bn.

Our people are our business. Talent is precious to us and we create an environment in which individuals can reach their full potential, unhindered by hierarchy. Our team comprises more than 65+ nationalities and we are committed to developing and sustaining a diverse work force.

Learn more about us here. This role is located in Houston, TX onsite 5x a week

Job Description

As our portfolio of work continues to grow, we are looking for an experienced Machine Learning Engineer to join our AI and machine learning team. The individual will work closely with AI, data and machine learning specialists, software engineers and commercial teams to deliver machine learning models and applications. We work across the trading business, operations, and other support functions; so the individual will need to be comfortable working with a variety of stakeholders and technologies. The successful candidate will bring a strong machine learning background and have extended this expertise through hands-on delivery of GenAI projects.

The Machine Learning Engineer at Vitol has visibility and impact across the full project workflow: from working with business stakeholders to help define the project, to data collation and processing, exploratory analysis, model selection and tuning, and implementation of production models.

The successful candidate will join a team of experienced, collaborative practitioners, who are (pragmatically) solving some of the most challenging and impactful problems the energy industry is facing; as well as pushing the boundaries around the ‘art of the possible’.

Core Responsibilities include:

Design, develop, and deploy end-to-end machine learning and data science solutions across our wider business activities (including trading, operations, and support functions) - from raw data ingestion through to production-grade models and monitoring
Drive adoption and development of the firm's internal GenAI platform and applications, extending capabilities through new integrations, data connectors, and domain-specific context engineering; work closely with trading desks and operational teams to identify high-value use cases, embed the tool into day-to-day workflows, and ensure outputs are robust, and trusted by end users.
Design, prototype, and deploy agentic LLM workflows, including tool use and function calling; develop reusable prompts and AI Skills integrated into business workflows
Evaluate and benchmark LLM and agentic solutions, engaging regularly with stakeholders to gather feedback and refine solutions
Apply a broad range of modelling techniques - including time-series forecasting, NLP, classification, and generative AI - to commodity pricing, supply/demand signals, trade flow analysis, and operational optimisation problems
Own the full data science and machine learning lifecycle on assigned projects: data sourcing and cleaning, exploratory analysis, feature engineering, model selection and validation, deployment, and ongoing performance monitoring
Build and maintain robust, well-tested, production-quality code; contribute to shared infrastructure including ML pipelines, data orchestration, and model serving layers
Integrate ML and GenAI outputs into existing trading systems, dashboards, and workflows; work with software engineers to ensure reliable, scalable adoption across the business
Communicate analytical findings and model outputs clearly to non-technical stakeholders; present results, assumptions, and limitations in a manner that supports confident commercial decision-making
Actively participate in code reviews, experiment design, and tooling decisions; mentor colleagues and help raise the overall standard of analytical and engineering practice across the team

Qualifications

Master’s degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Data Science, or a related quantitative field
Fluency in Python for both data science and engineering purposes: clean, modular, well-documented code, with strong understanding of software engineering best practices including version control, testing, and code review
5+ years of industry experience developing and deploying machine learning or statistical models, with a proven track record of delivering end-to-end solutions in production environments
Demonstrable experience applying a broad range of ML methodologies (supervised and unsupervised learning, time-series modelling, NLP/LLMs, optimisation) to real-world business problems
Strong proficiency with ML frameworks (e.g. PyTorch, scikit-learn, Transformers) and experience building or consuming LLM-based pipelines and GenAI applications. Hands-on delivery of GenAI projects, including prompt engineering and agentic patterns such as tool use and function calling
Experience with cloud platforms (AWS preferred) and modern MLOps practices: containerisation (Docker/Kubernetes), CI/CD, data pipeline orchestration (e.g. Airflow, Dagster), and model serving
Strong analytical and problem-solving ability: capable of defining and scoping open-ended problems, proposing sound methodological approaches, and defending modelling choices with rigorous reasoning
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to present model outputs, caveats, and commercial implications clearly to non-technical audiences including traders and senior management
Genuine intellectual curiosity about commodities markets, global energy flows, and the commercial dynamics of trading; willingness to develop domain knowledge as part of the role

Desirable Experience

Experience in the energy or commodities trading industry, with knowledge of financial markets and trading concepts
Experience surfacing ML outputs through interactive tools (e.g. Dash, Streamlit, or similar) and presenting use cases to non-technical audiences, including traders and senior management
Time-series modelling in a trading or financial context, including both ML-based and econometric approaches (e.g. ARIMA, cointegration, regime-switching models)
Experience building retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines or multi-agent systems
Experience building Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers or clients
Data orchestrators (Airflow, Dagster) and cloud-based ETL/ELT pipelines
Prior work on LLM evaluations (evals) or model benchmarking

Personal Characteristics

A self-motivated individual who thrives on seeing the results of their work make an impact in the business
Curiosity for emerging AI developments, with a proactive commitment to continuously learning, experimenting and expanding your skills
Pragmatic and delivery-focused: comfortable navigating ambiguity, balancing rigor with speed, and making sound judgements under uncertainty
Methodical and detail-oriented: rigorous in experimental design, data validation, and code quality, with a disciplined approach to documenting assumptions and results
Resourceful, able to think creatively and adapt in a dynamic environment
Team player, with an open non-political style and a high level of integrity
Desire to be a thought-partner in a fast-growing team, and make an impact at a business that sits at the heart of the world’s energy flows

Additional Information

What we offer

Large diversity of projects with real-world impacts on a truly global scale
Entrepreneurial environment within a flat hierarchy, where great ideas come to life quickly
Close collaboration with various business units across our key regions (eg. London, Singapore, Houston, Geneva)
A highly motivated DS and ML team comprised of experienced individuals with a supportive attitude and great team spirit
Being part of the energy transition through increased emphasis on renewable & alternative energy sources at a pivotal moment in the industry
Strong management commitment to incorporating machine learning into the future of Vitol’s operations

Comprehensive benefit coverage includes:

Medical

jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.description:
About Us

Mintive helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. That has to start from trust. Our first product is an MCP gateway that gives those agents governed access to company data and tools.

Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. Our gateway product scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on.

We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how.

We are AI-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team and handle sales, marketing, deal ops, and engineering on the same gateway we sell to customers, and we are building an entire company operating system around them.

Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 50+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. Our founders are machine learning experts from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU, with applied research at Google Brain and Waymo, and one co-founded Coursera.

The Job

You will own features end to end, from conception to production, across our gateway infrastructure, enterprise deployments, and agentic systems. The work leans backend and infra, but nothing is off limits: when the product needs a better UI you build it, and when a connector breaks during a security review you fix it.

Claude and Codex are your primary working environment, and you use a fleet of agents to move faster than a team this size has any right to. Agents write much of the code and review PRs, so your real job is the judgment they cannot make: shaping the problem, making architecture, product, and UX calls, hardening enterprise paths, designing connectors, protecting security-sensitive surfaces, and catching generated code that is quietly wrong. Roles are blurred and we ship within hours, and you will learn directly from the founders and from customers.

We hire across levels, from strong early-career builders to seasoned engineers, and we set level and pay to match. What matters most is judgment, range, and how fast you ship.

About You

You are a builder with a track record of shipping to real users, whether that is a product, an internal tool, an open-source project, or a serious side project. You ship, then iterate, without waiting for specs or approvals.
You have strong fundamentals and learn fast. How quickly you pick things up matters as much as years of experience.
You care about product value and customer needs over technical purity.
You take infra seriously. You think about blast radius, trust boundaries, and what happens when your code is in the path of every customer's agents.
You can read unfamiliar code, reason from first principles, and explain your tradeoffs.
You are comfortable across the stack (TypeScript, Python, CockroachDB), or you pick up new languages, protocols, and domains fast.
You are excited to build with agents, and to learn when they help and when they hide a problem.
You already build with AI every day and want room to move without heavy process.

Nice to have:

Developer-facing products, protocol or gateway work, or infrastructure at scale.
Background in security, identity, or permission systems.
Contributions to open source, MCP servers, or agentic frameworks.
Design sensibility: engineers who care about design, designers who think about infrastructure.

What we offer:

Competitive compensation and meaningful equity.
Unusual scope and ownership of features that ship to enterprise customers.
Building and deploying agents on the same platform we sell.
Direct access to the founders, customer context, and product direction, with mentorship as you grow.
Health benefits, on a team that puts family and health first.

Prefer to have your agent apply? Point it at https://www.mintmcp.com/hiring/mcp

We’re on a mission to redefine how modern distributed systems are tested and released. Our platform is trusted by engineering teams who demand rock-solid reliability, scalable performance, and deep technical visibility. Our platform doesn’t just assure system correctness and reliability, it exists because developers need something better. If you’ve ever experienced the pain of a production outage, had a bad week on-call, or had a release delayed by weeks because of one killer bug – you’ll understand exactly why we’re doing what we do. If you're passionate about developer-first products, system resilience, and correctness, we’d love to talk.

About The Role

We’re hiring an Applied AI Software Engineer to build AI native products, integrations, API management, and more, that help our Finance and Accounting teams. Finance here spans FP&A, Accounting, Tax, Payroll, Reporting, SalesOps, Treasury, Equity Management, AP, AR, and Finance/Accounting Ops. The team is moving fast as the company scales, and there’s a big opportunity to automate the remaining manual work and free them up for higher value work.

You’ll work at the intersection of software engineering, applied AI, data, and Finance operations.

What You’ll Do

Work directly with Finance and Accounting to understand how they work, where they get stuck, and how they could do more with technology.
Design, build, and ship full stack products that use AI to help non technical teams get work done.
Build everything from lightweight agent workflows and automations to production applications for reporting, reconciliation, close support, and other Finance and Accounting problems.

Partner with Finance, Accounting, and RevOps to integrate with the systems they use, like our ERP and Salesforce.

Keep AI work from being siloed. Today it lives with individuals on the team; help turn it into shared tools, reports, and a source of truth that can be maintained and audited as we grow.
Support globalization and the expansion of the Finance team.

Why Join Us?

Join a collaborative, kind team supporting a rapidly growing company.
Work with the resources - tools, teammates, and world-class experts - to do portfolio worthy work.
Use and explore AI in an environment that does not tolerate workslop.

Preferred Qualifications

4+ years of professional software engineering experience, including independently shipping and operating production systems.
Experience shipping an LLM powered product, feature, or workflow for real users. You understand the difference between an impressive prototype and a system people can depend on.
Experience working directly with non technical users to understand their workflows, test ideas, and improve products through feedback.

Strong product and engineering judgment. You can move quickly when the problem calls for an experiment and build for reliability, auditability, and access control when the solution becomes business critical.

Our current stack for internal applications includes TypeScript, React, and AWS. Experience with these tools is helpful, but we care more about strong engineering fundamentals and the ability to learn.

CPA

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Full-Stack ML Infrastructure
jobs.description:
Company

Pramaana Labs is a frontier AI lab building the verification layer for AI. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in Palo Alto, we turn complex human knowledge, including tax codes, legal rules, clinical guidelines and security protocols, into a formal representation, so every AI answer can be traced, challenged, and proved. Pramaana's architecture pairs foundation models trained to formalize and reason with a symbolic world model encoded in Lean 4. Pramaana was founded by a team out of Google, DeepMind, and Glean, combining frontier AI researchers and formal methods experts.

The Role

We’re looking for a full-stack engineer with focus on infrastructure to build the tools and systems that help Pramaana’s engineers and researchers develop, test, deploy, and operate their work more effectively.

Your initial focus will be DevOps and MLOps
: improving development environments and deployment workflows, making experiments and evaluations reproducible, and helping teams understand the behavior, performance, and cost of AI systems. You’ll build across interfaces, backend services, and infrastructure automation—not just maintain scripts or configure dashboards.

This is an early-stage role with scope across the company. As needs evolve, your work will extend into shared capabilities such as identity and access, LLM gateways, API-key management, training and inference platform maintenance, usage metering, and internal applications. You’ll work directly with the people using these systems, turning recurring friction into reliable, self-serve tools.

We’re looking for someone who treats internal tools as products: useful, understandable, well-maintained, and built around the workflows of the people who depend on them.

What You'll Do

Improve how software gets built and deployed. Develop repeatable local environments, automated tests, CI/CD pipelines, and deployment workflows. Help make configuration, secrets, releases, and rollbacks easier to manage safely.
Build tools for the AI development lifecycle. Create workflows for running experiments and evaluations, versioning datasets and configurations, tracking results and artifacts, and deploying or integrating model services. Make runs easier to reproduce, compare, and investigate. Help researchers get from a recipe to a running job, and from a failed job to the cause..
Create full-stack, self-serve applications. Build interfaces and APIs that let teams launch jobs, manage configurations, inspect results, and troubleshoot failures without relying on repeated manual assistance.
Make systems observable and costs understandable. Connect logs, metrics, traces, and usage data so teams can diagnose issues, identify bottlenecks, and understand where time and compute are being spent.
Contribute to shared platform services. Help build and integrate identity, access controls, LLM routing, API keys, budgets, and usage metering across Pramaana’s products and internal workflows.
Use existing tools thoughtfully. Evaluate and extend open-source or managed solutions where they fit. Build custom software where it solves a real gap, rather than recreating infrastructure unnecessarily.
Improve tools through direct feedback. Work alongside engineers and researchers to identify recurring problems, prioritize improvements, and measure whether tools reduce setup time, manual work, and failed runs. Maintain tests, documentation, and operational guidance for what you ship.

You Will Thrive in This Role If You Have

Minimum 2-3 years of software engineering experience, including hands-on work with backend services, full-stack applications, internal tools, or deployment automation.
A solid foundation in building software across the stack. You can develop services and automation in Python or TypeScript, work with APIs and databases, and build usable interfaces with React or a similar framework.
Practical cloud and deployment experience. You’ve deployed applications using containers and a cloud platform such as AWS, worked with CI/CD, and used logs or metrics to investigate problems.
Some hands-on exposure to AI or ML workflows. This could include integrating model APIs, running evaluations, tracking experiments, or operating model-backed applications through work or substantial projects. You don’t need to be an ML researcher.
A product mindset for internal users. You care about clear interfaces, sensible defaults, useful documentation, and reducing the number of steps it takes someone to get their work done.
Good engineering judgment and a collaborative approach. You write maintainable code, test important behavior, ask for review, and communicate trade-offs. You can take ownership of a scoped problem while recognizing when to seek help.

Especially Strong Candidates May Also Have

Experience with experiment tracking, evaluation pipelines, workflow orchestration, or model observability using tools such as MLflow, Langfuse, or Temporal.
Experience with infrastructure as code, container orchestration, or telemetry tooling, such as Terraform, Kubernetes, or OpenTelemetry.
Experience running GPU workloads on Kubernetes: job queueing and preemption multi-node training with NCCL over EFA or InfiniBand, GPU node health and driver management, or serving models with vLLM or SGLang.
Experience implementing authentication, role-based access, API-key management, image provenance, LLM gateways, usage and cost tracking or hardening public endpoints.
Experience adapting open-source software or building developer tools that other engineers or researchers use regularly.

You don’t need experience with every system listed above. Strong software engineering fundamentals, practical problem-solving, and an interest in DevOps and MLOps matter more than matching every tool.

jobs.description:
The Company

AnySignal is developing the next generation of RF products and services for some of the most demanding space and defense missions. We’re building a flexible, high-performance platform that’s easy to deploy, monitor, and scale, enabling customers to bring advanced radio technologies to life faster than ever before.

The Role

We’re hiring an Embedded Software Engineer to develop the software that controls and operates our ground antenna systems.

This role sits at the intersection of software and electromechanical systems. You will develop software that controls antenna motion, motors, actuators, sensors, and other components, integrate new electrical and mechanical systems into the ground software stack, and work closely with mechanical, electrical, RF, and software engineers to build and operate reliable ground systems.

Responsibilities

Develop software that supports the operation and integration of ground antenna systems
Develop reliable, low-level software for controlling motors, actuators, sensors, and other electromechanical components
Build and maintain interfaces between software and ground-station systems using low-level communication protocols
Integrate and test new electrical and mechanical systems with the antenna software stack
Troubleshoot software and electromechanical behavior across integrated systems
Develop automated tests and tools to validate antenna control software and system performance
Work closely with mechanical, electrical, RF, and software engineers to bring new ground-station capabilities into operation
Support the deployment and reliable operation of ground antenna systems in the field

What We're Looking For

Must-Haves:

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field
Strong software development experience in Python
Strong experience developing software in Embedded Linux environments
Experience with networking and software communication protocols
Professional experience developing and debugging software that integrates with motors, actuators, servos, encoders, sensors, controllers, or other electromechanical systems
Experience developing and debugging low-level interfaces and communication protocols
Experience with test automation and software validation
Ability to work cross-functionally with software, electrical, mechanical, and RF engineers

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience developing software in C or C++
Experience with RF systems, satellite communications, or ground-station systems
Experience deploying or supporting integrated software/electromechanical systems in field environments
Experience with GNU Radio or similar software-defined radio frameworks

Compensation

The estimated base salary range for this role is $130,000-$200,000 per year, plus equity. This range reflects our good-faith estimate for this position at the time of posting. The final base salary offered will depend on a variety of factors, including the candidate's qualifications, relevant experience, skills, and market considerations.

In addition to base salary and equity, AnySignal offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) program, competitive paid time off, and paid parental leave.

jobs.title: Python Automation Engineer (PAM)
jobs.description:
Python Automation Engineer

Phoenix, AZ (Hybrid – 3 days in office)

PAM Engineer – Job Description Breakdown & Recruiter Guide

The short version

This is a Python automation engineer who works in privileged access management (PAM), not a pure CyberArk administrator.
Companies have powerful accounts (admin logins, database credentials, service accounts) that could give an attacker access to everything if stolen. PAM locks those accounts in a secure vault, controls who can use them, records what they do, and rotates the passwords automatically. This person keeps that system running and writes code so it runs with less manual effort.

Who this person is, in one sentence:
a security-minded software or systems engineer who understands identity and access, writes solid Python, and can run their own projects, ideally with some CyberArk experience.
What they'd do day to day

The job splits into four kinds of work:
Operate the PAM environment:
onboard accounts into the vault, fix things that break, handle access requests, and keep the system healthy.
Automate:
write Python (plus PowerShell or Bash) scripts and integrations so tasks once done by hand happen automatically.
Run projects independently:
take an assignment from kickoff to delivery without much hand-holding.
Integrate systems:
connect the PAM tool to identity platforms such as Okta or Microsoft Entra ID through APIs.

CyberArk is the product this client uses; the rest of the terms below are its parts or the systems it connects to.
Term

What it means

CyberArk
The leading PAM software product. This is the tool the client uses.
Digital Vault
The secure "safe" where privileged passwords and secrets are stored.
CPM (Central Policy Manager)
Automatically changes and verifies passwords on a schedule.
PSM (Privileged Session Manager)
Proxies and records admin sessions, creating an audit trail.
PVWA (Password Vault Web Access)
The web interface people use to request and retrieve access.
Okta / Entra ID / Auth0
Identity platforms that handle login and single sign-on.
REST API
The standard way software systems talk to each other, and how most of the automation gets built.
AD / LDAP
Directory systems that store users and groups.
AI / ML / LLM familiarity
Using AI to spot unusual privileged activity or analyze logs. A "nice to understand" item, not the core of the job.
How to read the requirements

Programming ability and independent delivery are the real core; CyberArk is a bonus, and the long bullet list is a wish list that almost no one fully matches.
Programming is the core.
Python is the first bullet, and the posting repeats "independent" and "end-to-end" several times. They want a builder who owns outcomes, not only an administrator.
CyberArk is "preferred, not mandatory."
A strong Python and identity/security engineer who can learn CyberArk is acceptable. This is the biggest lever for widening the candidate pool.
Treat most of the list as bonuses.
Screen hard on the must-haves below and weigh the rest as differentiators.

Must-haves (screen hard)

Production Python, with design, debugging, and maintenance owned independently
Independent end-to-end project delivery
REST API design, integration, and security
IAM and privileged access fundamentals, plus AD/LDAP and authentication protocols (Kerberos, SAML, OIDC)
Git, plus PowerShell or Bash scripting

Strong differentiators

Hands-on CyberArk experience (PVWA, CPM, PSM, Digital Vault), especially the CyberArk REST API and CPM plugin or PSM connector development
Okta, Entra ID, or Auth0 integration experience
Applied AI/LLM work in security operations, such as log analysis, anomaly detection, or risk scoring

jobs.description:
Company

Pramaana Labs is a frontier AI lab building the verification layer for AI. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in Palo Alto, we turn complex human knowledge, including tax codes, legal rules, clinical guidelines and security protocols, into a formal representation, so every AI answer can be traced, challenged, and proved. Pramaana's architecture pairs foundation models trained to formalize and reason with a symbolic world model encoded in Lean 4. Pramaana was founded by a team out of Google, DeepMind, and Glean, combining frontier AI researchers and formal methods experts.

The Role

We’re looking for a full-stack Product Engineer to turn Pramaana’s research into products that customers and developers can use and trust. You’ll make complex reasoning accessible through intuitive interfaces and thoughtful developer experiences, helping users understand, inspect, and verify AI outputs.

This is a hands-on, early-stage role spanning customer-facing applications, developer APIs, and new product experiments. You won’t be confined to one feature or product. You’ll help discover what users need, build the experience across the stack, and improve it through real-world use.

You’ll work closely with product, design, engineering, and research, taking ownership of projects from the MVP through production. We’re looking for someone who cares about both how AI works and how people experience it - and who enjoys making complex technology feel straightforward.

What You'll Do

Build complete product experiences. Take problems from initial exploration to working software, owning the frontend, backend, data models, integrations, and testing needed to deliver a useful result.
Create thoughtful, responsive interfaces. Build workflows that help users bring in knowledge, review rules, ask questions, and inspect results and supporting evidence. Pay attention to interaction details, accessibility, loading states, and errors.
Develop reliable APIs and services. Build the systems behind document processing, asynchronous jobs, verification workflows, and customer integrations. Make progress, failures, and recovery understandable to users.
Turn research capabilities into usable products. Partner with researchers to integrate models, agents, and verification services. Help bridge the gap between a promising technical demonstration and an experience customers can depend on.
Learn directly from users. Work with customers and internal stakeholders to understand their workflows, test assumptions, and identify useful improvements. Instrument features and use feedback and usage data to guide iteration.
Own quality beyond launch. Write tests, review code, monitor the features you ship, and investigate production issues. Improve performance, security, and reliability as usage grows.
Build foundations that support multiple products. Create reusable components, services, and integration patterns. Make practical decisions about what to share, what to keep simple, and when a prototype needs a more durable implementation.

You Will Thrive in This Role If You Have

Minimum 2–3 years of software engineering experience, with examples of products or features you’ve shipped and improved. We value meaningful hands-on ownership more than a particular title or background.
Strong full-stack fundamentals. You’re comfortable building interfaces with TypeScript and React, backend services with Python or Node.js, and working with APIs and relational databases. You may be stronger on one side of the stack, but you’re willing to work across both.
Product judgment and attention to detail. You think about the user’s goal, question unnecessary complexity, and care whether the final experience is understandable—not just technically functional.
Practical experience delivering production software. You’re familiar with testing, version control, code review, deployment, and debugging. You understand the basics of authentication, authorization, and handling user data responsibly.
Comfort working through ambiguity. You can break a loosely defined problem into manageable steps, test an approach, and adjust as you learn.
Ownership, curiosity, and clear communication. You follow through on what you build, surface problems early, and work well with people across engineering, design, product, and research.

Especially Strong Candidates May Also Have

Experience building applications with LLM APIs, retrieval, agent workflows, or evaluation systems.
Experience with enterprise software, developer tools, or workflows involving complex documents, structured knowledge, or auditable decisions.
Strong frontend craft, including experience building editors, data visualizations, or other information-rich interfaces.
Experience taking a startup product, substantial side project, or open-source tool from an idea to active users.

Prior experience in formal verification is not required. We’re looking for strong builders who are curious about the technology and motivated to make it useful.

jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern, 3D & Manufacturing Applications
jobs.description:
About Valstad

Valstad is building the machine that builds the ships.

We combine industrial robotics, welding, sensing, and AI to turn 3D models into real high-mix ship structure. Our mission is to rapidly expand America's maritime output by 100x.

Our team works directly with large industrial robots and real manufacturing equipment at our Austin facility. The systems we build will ultimately be deployed across shipyards and industrial facilities throughout the country.

About Valstad

Valstad is rebuilding how ships are made.

American shipbuilding is constrained by slow, labor-intensive production methods and a shortage of skilled manufacturing capacity. We are developing robotic production systems that can turn engineering data directly into finished steel structures, dramatically reducing the time and manual programming required to build ships.

Our first platform combines industrial robots, automated material handling, welding, sensing and AI-driven manufacturing software to produce large ship panels and structural assemblies. Instead of programming each new part by hand, our goal is for the system to understand the CAD model, determine how the structure should be assembled and welded, and generate the robotic plan required to build it.

This requires software that allows engineers and operators to understand complex 3D structures, review automatically generated manufacturing plans, control production workflows and respond when physical conditions differ from the nominal CAD model.

The software you build will be used to manufacture real steel structures in our Austin facility and, over time, in shipyards across the country.

The Internship

Valstad is seeking a Software Engineering Intern to help build interactive 3D and manufacturing applications for our robotic production platform.

You will work with CAD-derived geometry, robot paths, manufacturing data and factory workflows. Depending on your experience and interests, your project may involve 3D visualization, CAD-model processing, manufacturing-plan review, production interfaces or tools for analyzing robotic operations.

This is not an internship centered on mock projects or isolated coding exercises. You will own a defined software capability, work directly with engineers and factory users, and deliver something intended for use by the team.

You will be paired with a technical mentor and will participate in normal engineering planning, code review, testing and deployment processes.

Potential Projects

Your primary project will be selected based on your experience and Valstad’s highest-priority needs. Possible projects include:

Building an interactive 3D viewer for ship panels, stiffeners, welds, fixtures and robotic operations
Visualizing robot paths, tool orientations, work envelopes and manufacturing sequences
Developing model-selection, filtering, measurement, annotation and section-view tools
Building a CAD-import validation interface that identifies missing geometry, incorrect units or unsupported model conditions
Developing tools for comparing model revisions and identifying affected manufacturing operations
Building production job-status and operator interfaces
Creating visualizations for coordinate frames, transformations and sensor measurements
Developing tools for reviewing the difference between nominal CAD geometry and measured physical geometry
Building dashboards for robot faults, manual interventions, cycle times and production outcomes
Improving the performance of large 3D models through instancing, level of detail or incremental loading
Creating automated tests for complex manufacturing workflows
Developing internal tools that connect CAD entities to manufacturing and inspection records

What You Will Do

Design and implement a scoped software project from initial requirements through demonstration and deployment.
Build production-quality frontend or full-stack software.
Work with manufacturing, robotics and welding engineers to understand real operational requirements.
Observe how software is used in Valstad’s manufacturing facility.
Work with CAD-derived geometry and manufacturing data.
Develop clear user interfaces for complex technical workflows.
Write automated tests and participate in code review.
Diagnose software behavior using logs, production data and user feedback.
Document your work so the system can be maintained and extended after the internship.
Present your completed project to the broader Valstad team.

Required Qualifications

Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, software engineering, computer engineering or a related field.
Strong programming fundamentals.
Experience building software outside of introductory coursework.
Experience with JavaScript or TypeScript.
Familiarity with a modern frontend framework such as React, Vue or Svelte.
Ability to work independently on a clearly defined technical project.
Strong debugging and problem-solving skills.
Ability to communicate clearly and ask useful technical questions.
Interest in robotics, manufacturing, CAD, graphics or industrial software.
Availability to work full-time and on-site in Austin for the duration of the internship.

Strongly Preferred

Experience with React and TypeScript.
Experience with Three.js, React Three Fiber, Babylon.js, WebGL or another real-time 3D graphics framework.
Experience developing CAD, CAM, BIM, simulation or engineering applications.
Familiarity with meshes, coordinate systems, transformations or computational geometry.
Experience with Python, C++, Rust, Go or another backend or systems language.
Experience with PostgreSQL, APIs or backend application development.
Experience working with STEP, IGES, STL, OBJ, glTF, DXF or similar geometry formats.
Experience with Open Cascade or another geometry-processing library.
Experience building applications for technical or expert users.
Experience deploying a real application used by people other than yourself.
Participation in research, student robotics, Formula SAE, engineering design teams or relevant open-source projects.

What We Look For

We are less interested in a specific number of completed courses than in evidence that you can build useful software.

Strong candidates often have:

Personal projects with meaningful technical depth
Open-source contributions
Research or laboratory experience
Previous technical internships
Student-team experience
A portfolio or GitHub profile showing completed work
A strong explanation of the tradeoffs and failures encountered while building something

Shipbuilding experience is not required. We care about technical curiosity, product judgment and the ability to turn complex requirements into reliable software.

What Success Looks Like

By the end of the internship, you will have delivered a working software capability that improves how Valstad’s team plans, visualizes or executes robotic manufacturing.

Your project will have:

A clearly defined user and purpose
Production-quality implementation
Automated tests appropriate to the project
Documentation and a clear handoff
Feedback from actual engineers or factory users
A final demonstration using real or representative manufacturing data

The strongest interns may be considered for future internships or full-time positions.

Compensation And Benefits

The anticipated pay range for this internship is $32 to $38 per hour
, depending on experience and technical depth.

The internship also includes:

A dedicated technical mentor
Direct exposure to industrial robots and manufacturing operations
Ownership of a substantive engineering project
Regular feedback and code review
Potential relocation or temporary-housing assistance where appropriate
Consideration for future internship or full-time opportunities

Valstad is an equal-opportunity employer. We evaluate candidates based on their ability, experience and potential to contribute to the company’s mission.

Develop generative models that improve how machine learning models are trained and evaluated on real-world sensing data.

Direct collaboration with the founding team, competitive hourly pay, top-tier VC backing, and a rare opportunity to help build a "Zero to One" technology company at the intersection of AI, wearables, and real-world human behavior understanding. new_jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer - New Grad
new_jobs.description:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.
About the Team The Machine Learning team builds the model-side techniques that make SambaNova’s platform fast and capable. We train speculative decoding models that accelerate inference, develop efficient ML methods such as quantization, sparsity, and distillation, and build agentic systems on top of our foundation model serving stack. Our work spans research, applied science, and production, from novel approach design to proofs of concept and shipping to product. Reinforcement learning and post-training are within our scope and a growing part of our roadmap.
About the Role As a new grad Machine Learning Engineer, you’ll train and evaluate models that make large language models cheaper and more capable to serve. Depending on your interests, that could mean training speculator (draft) models and tuning acceptance rates, compressing models without losing accuracy, or designing and evaluating agentic workflows for tool use, planning, and long-horizon tasks. You’ll work closely with the AI performance, compiler, and runtime teams to turn research results into measured end-to-end wins, and you’ll have room to pursue open problems as our reinforcement learning and post-training work ramps up.
Responsibilities Train, evaluate, and tune speculative decoding models (Dspark/Dflash, Medusa/Eagle-style heads, and multi-token prediction) to increase acceptance rates on production workloads.
Develop and implement optimization techniques, including quantization, sparsity, distillation, pruning, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning, to quantify the trade-offs between model quality, latency, and resource efficiency.
Build and evaluate agentic systems: tool calling, multi-step planning, retrieval, and long-context reasoning on top of our serving stack.
Design rigorous evaluations and benchmarks; make accuracy and quality claims that hold up under scrutiny
Translate recent research into working implementations, and run ablations to understand what actually drives the result
Partner with the AI performance, compiler, runtime, and product teams to ship model improvements into SambaNova products
Contribute to emerging areas such as reinforcement learning, post-training, and reward modeling as the roadmap expands

Required Qualifications B.S. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
Strong programming skills in Python
Solid foundation in machine learning, linear algebra, probability, and numerical computing
Hands-on experience with PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX
Working knowledge of transformer architectures and the LLM training or inference pipeline
Ability to design a clean experiment, interpret results honestly, and communicate findings clearly

Preferred Qualifications M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field
Research or internship experience in LLM training, post-training, or inference
Experience with speculative decoding, distillation, quantization, sparsity, or other model efficiency techniques
Experience building agentic systems, tool-calling pipelines, or LLM evaluation harnesses
Familiarity with reinforcement learning or preference optimization (RLHF, DPO, GRPO, reward modeling)
Experience with distributed training frameworks (FSDP, DeepSpeed, Megatron) or inference frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM
Publications at ML venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP) or meaningful open source contributions

Base Salary Range:
Base Pay Range: $131,200 USD - $196,800 USD
Submission Guidelines

Please note that in order to be considered an applicant for any position at SambaNova Systems, you must submit an application form for each position for which you believe you are qualified.

new_jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer
new_jobs.description:
Machine Learning Engineers
at IMC play a pivotal role in building the systems that drive training and deployment of large-scale ML models across IMC's global operations. They collaborate with quantitative researchers, hardware specialists and software engineers to build robust systems that get the most out of GPU acceleration, distributed computing and the broader open-source ML ecosystem. ML Engineers' work directly shapes how fast we can experiment, iterate and deploy — accelerating the cycle that turns a research idea into a live trading strategy.

This is a unique opportunity to solve problems at the intersection of advanced machine learning and trading, where your contributions will shape the future of IMC's technology and trading capabilities.

As a team, our Machine Learning Engineers broadly work across two areas: ML Research Engineering
, focused on the systems and frameworks researchers use to train, evaluate and iterate on models at scale; and ML Performance Engineering
, focused on making ML workloads execute as efficiently as possible, typically through GPU and low-level systems optimization. These aren't rigid tracks, and there is overlap between them. You will bring depth of expertise in at least one of these focus areas and collaborate closely with global team members.

Your Core Responsibilities

The responsibilities below are representative of the role — the exact mix depends on your team, area of expertise and location.

ML Research Engineering

Develop large-scale distributed training pipelines that manage complex datasets and models.
Partner with quantitative researchers to automate ML experiments, hyperparameter tuning and model retraining.
Work with HPC specialists to optimise workflows, improve training speed and reduce compute cost.

ML Performance Engineering

Build and optimise low-latency inference pipelines, ensuring models deliver real-time predictions in production systems.
Maximise performance in training and inference using GPU hardware and acceleration libraries.

Across both areas

Extend and improve the internals of machine learning frameworks and open-source tools to raise their performance for our workloads.
Design scalable model infrastructure capable of handling high-volume trading data and delivering real-time, high-accuracy predictions.
Evaluate and roll out third-party tools that enhance model development, training and inference capabilities.

Your Skills And Experience

Core, regardless of focus area:

3+ years of experience in machine learning, with a focus on training or inference systems.
Production software engineering — Python, testing discipline and genuine ownership of systems once they ship.
Machine learning fundamentals — you understand modern ML workloads beyond high-level APIs and can reason about model behaviour, correctness and performance at the level relevant to your area of expertise.
A systems mindset — you reach for measurement before opinion on performance, scale or reliability issues, and can make sound build-versus-buy decisions.
Strong collaboration — comfortable explaining the reasoning behind your technical decisions, working through differing perspectives with researchers and adapting your approach when the evidence supports it.

Depth In One Or More Of The Following

Distributed training and large-scale systems — parallelism strategy, data pipelines and checkpointing; frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow or JAX.
GPU performance and low-level optimisation — reasoning about memory, compute and latency at the device level, and optimising performance across kernels, compilers and hardware (e.g. CUDA, Triton or equivalent).
Production inference systems — hands-on experience building and hardening real-time, low-latency prediction pipelines in high-performance environments.
Numerics and correctness at scale — low-precision effects, KV caching, batching, and knowing which optimisations stay bit-exact.

Technologies listed above are examples rather than requirements; equivalent depth developed using other stacks or hardware platforms is equally relevant.

Also a Plus

Exposure to cloud platforms and orchestration tools.
A track record of contributing to open-source projects in machine learning, data science or distributed systems.

Not sure this is the one?
If your strength is mainly in modelling and research direction, our Deep Learning Researcher roles are likely a closer fit. If your strength is in general infrastructure rather than ML-specific systems, take a look at our broader infrastructure engineering roles.

The Base Salary range for the role is included below. Base salary is only one component of total compensation; all full-time, permanent positions are eligible for a discretionary bonus and benefits, including paid leave and insurance. Please visit Benefits - US | IMC Trading for more comprehensive information.

Salary Range

$175,000 - $250,000 USD

About Us

IMC is a research-driven trading firm where quantitative modeling, machine learning, and engineering shape how modern markets are traded. A stabilizing force in markets since 1989, we provide liquidity across trading venues, delivering the best outcome in value and risk management to investors. Using our own technology and capital, we build proprietary systems and algorithms that operate across global markets. Our researchers, traders, and engineers work as a collective, combining rapid experimentation, advanced infrastructure, and real-time feedback to turn insight into execution and execution into advantage.

Machine Learning Engineer | AI Security & Fraud Detection

Location:
San Francisco, CA - Onsite
Compensation:
$220,000–$300,000

3+ Years, Ideally 5+ Years
Industry:
AI Infrastructure, Agentic AI, Cybersecurity, Fraud Prevention

About the Opportunity

Shields Group Search is partnering with a well-funded, early-stage AI infrastructure startup building the trust and security layer for the rapidly emerging AI agent economy.
As AI agents increasingly act autonomously on behalf of individuals and businesses, from booking services and accessing APIs to executing financial transactions, companies need infrastructure that can determine which agents are legitimate, who they represent, what actions they're authorized to perform, and whether their behavior presents a security or fraud risk.
Our client is building real-time verification and decisioning infrastructure that enables businesses to safely interact with AI agents at scale.
The platform combines agent identity verification, behavioral intelligence, risk assessment, and security controls to distinguish legitimate automated activity from suspicious or malicious behavior.

We're looking for an exceptional Machine Learning Engineer to build the models that distinguish a trusted AI agent from an attack, in real time and under load.

This is an opportunity to join a small, highly technical founding-stage engineering team and take meaningful ownership of mission-critical ML infrastructure.
What You'll Be Working On
The models behind this platform operate directly on the production request path. They must evaluate activity and support trust decisions in real time, under the same strict latency constraints as the rest of the infrastructure.
There is no offline batch job to hide behind and no second chance if a prediction is too slow or incorrect.

You'll work on problems involving:

Real-Time Fraud & Threat Detection:
Develop ML models that identify potentially fraudulent, malicious, or unauthorized agent activity while minimizing false positives.
Behavioral & Anomaly Detection:
Identify suspicious patterns, anomalous agent interactions, and emerging risks across automated transactions and API activity.
Low-Latency ML Inference:
Build and optimize production model-serving systems capable of making accurate decisions under demanding latency and throughput requirements.
Cold-Start & Low-Label Learning:
Develop effective detection approaches when labeled examples are scarce, including unsupervised learning, weak supervision, and custom evaluation datasets.
End-to-End ML Ownership:
Build, evaluate, deploy, monitor, and continuously improve production ML systems, from data and feature pipelines through real-time serving.
Adversarial ML:
Help build systems that remain effective as malicious actors adapt their behavior to evade detection.
Agentic AI Infrastructure:
Work at the intersection of modern ML, AI agents, tool calling, identity verification, and security.

What We're Looking For

Must-Haves

3+ years of professional ML experience
, ideally 5+ years, building, evaluating, and deploying production models, not just research or notebooks.
Strong Python and a modern ML framework (PyTorch or TensorFlow); solid SQL.
Production ML systems end to end: feature pipelines, training, evaluation, and low-latency, real-time serving.
Comfort with low-label and cold-start problems, including anomaly detection, unsupervised methods, weak supervision, and building evaluation sets and labels from scratch.
Data analysis, statistics, and experiment design.
Strong software engineering. You ship versioned, testable, reproducible code, not throwaway models.
Experience working in highly technical engineering environments with strong software engineering standards.
Ability to take ownership, solve ambiguous problems, and ship production-grade solutions in a fast-moving startup environment.

Strongly Preferred

Applied ML in fraud, risk, abuse, account integrity, or security.
Experience building ML models for fraud prevention, threat detection, trust and safety, or other systems designed to prevent malicious activity.
Graph ML / GNNs, sequence or behavioral modeling, or anomaly detection.
LLM / NLP work, and familiarity with AI agents, including tool use, function calling, and MCP.
Experience in adversarial settings, where the threat evolves against the model.
Explainable, auditable, reproducible ML, with real model versioning.
Experience developing ML systems at highly technical, engineering-driven companies, particularly those working on large-scale infrastructure, payments, fraud prevention, cybersecurity, or AI platforms.

Bonus Qualifications

Payment protocols (x402), agent identity (DID / VC), or crypto commitments (Merkle anchoring).
Experience at an early-stage startup or building ML infrastructure from the ground up.
Familiarity with real-time transaction monitoring, behavioral risk scoring, or identity verification systems.

Compensation & Work Arrangement

$220,000–$300,000
Equity:
Competitive equity participation in an early-stage, venture-backed company.
Location:
San Francisco, CA.
Work Arrangement:
The team strongly prefers engineers working onsite five days per week. Hybrid flexibility may be considered for exceptional candidates who can regularly collaborate in person.
Start Date:
The team is hiring immediately and can move quickly for the right individual.

Vitol’s customers include national oil companies, multinationals, leading industrial companies and utilities. Founded in Rotterdam in 1966, today Vitol serves its customers from more than 40 offices worldwide. Revenues in 2025 were $343bn.

Our people are our business. Talent is precious to us and we create an environment in which individuals can reach their full potential, unhindered by hierarchy. Our team comprises more than 65+ nationalities and we are committed to developing and sustaining a diverse work force.

Learn more about us here. This role is located in Houston, TX onsite 5x a week

Job Description

As our portfolio of work continues to grow, we are looking for an experienced Machine Learning Engineer to join our AI and machine learning team. The individual will work closely with AI, data and machine learning specialists, software engineers and commercial teams to deliver machine learning models and applications. We work across the trading business, operations, and other support functions; so the individual will need to be comfortable working with a variety of stakeholders and technologies. The successful candidate will bring a strong machine learning background and have extended this expertise through hands-on delivery of GenAI projects.

The Machine Learning Engineer at Vitol has visibility and impact across the full project workflow: from working with business stakeholders to help define the project, to data collation and processing, exploratory analysis, model selection and tuning, and implementation of production models.

The successful candidate will join a team of experienced, collaborative practitioners, who are (pragmatically) solving some of the most challenging and impactful problems the energy industry is facing; as well as pushing the boundaries around the ‘art of the possible’.

Core Responsibilities include:

Design, develop, and deploy end-to-end machine learning and data science solutions across our wider business activities (including trading, operations, and support functions) - from raw data ingestion through to production-grade models and monitoring
Drive adoption and development of the firm's internal GenAI platform and applications, extending capabilities through new integrations, data connectors, and domain-specific context engineering; work closely with trading desks and operational teams to identify high-value use cases, embed the tool into day-to-day workflows, and ensure outputs are robust, and trusted by end users.

Experience building Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers or clients
